item.title: Arthur Russell
item.description: In the spring of 1979, the Kitchen’s former music director booked two nights of his own music into the room that minimalism had made its sanctum, and brought a drummer and two percussionists.

item.title: Curtis Mayfield
item.description: The sound that made Curtis Mayfield unmistakable was built from a child’s shortcut.

item.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto
item.description: As a Tokyo high schooler, Ryuichi Sakamoto rode a packed commuter train twenty minutes every morning and started counting the noise.

item.title: The Funk Brothers
item.description: The most prolific and least credited ensemble in the history of recorded music.

item.title: Holland-Dozier-Holland
item.description: The most prolific and commercially successful songwriting-production team in the history of Motown, and arguably the most important songwriting team of the 1960s after Lennon-McCartney.

item.title: Stevie Wonder
item.description: The riff that opens “Superstition” — that dirty, stacked Hohner Clavinet line — Stevie Wonder built alone, laying down the drums first and then overdubbing the keyboards and the vocal himself.
